title: Restoration of Alkaline and Sodic Soils via Gypsum and Halophyte Phytoremediation
source: ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute & FAO Land and Water Division
summary: High soil pH (> 8.5) and high Exchangeable Sodium Percentage (ESP > 15%) disperse clay platelets, sealing soil pores and suffocating root systems. Gypsum and organic leaching restore ionic equilibrium.

quantified_impact.soil_ph_neutralization: Reduction from pH 8.8-9.2 down to 7.6-8.0 over 18-24 months
quantified_impact.hydraulic_conductivity_recovery: 3.5x to 5x increase in water downward percolation rate

scientific_mechanism: Calcium ions (Ca2+) from gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) displace toxic monovalent sodium (Na+) bound to clay surfaces via cation exchange. The displaced Na+ forms soluble Na2SO4 and leaches below root zones during flooding or rainfall events. Flocculated Ca-clays restore crumb structure and macroporosity.
recommended_interventions: Calculate gypsum requirement based on ESP test (apply 3-6 t/ha finely powdered agricultural gypsum)
Establish deep green-manuring with Sesbania aculeata (Dhaincha) prior to main crop cycle
Incorporate composted pressmud or acidified organic matter to generate carbonic acid

title: On-Farm In-Situ Water Harvesting: Keyline Design and Contour Swales
source: World Overview of Conservation Approaches and Technologies (WOCAT) / FAO
summary: In low rainfall or semi-arid zones (< 600 mm/year), erratic intense downpours wash away topsoil. Earth contour bunds, swales, and Vetiver grass (Chrysopogon zizanioides) hedgerows intercept and infiltrate 80% of rainfall.

quantified_impact.soil_moisture_retention_duration: +35-55 days prolonged root-zone moisture availability into dry season
quantified_impact.topsoil_loss_prevention: 75-90% reduction in sediment transport per hectare
quantified_impact.shallow_aquifer_recharge: +22-38% rise in local water table levels over 3 hydrological cycles

scientific_mechanism: Contour swales convert kinetic energy of overland sheet flow into potential energy, slowing down velocity (Manning's equation). Still water infiltrates horizontally beneath the trench ridge, forming a subterranean moisture plume (hydration lens) accessible to deep-rooted crops and companion trees.
recommended_interventions: Excavate level contour swales spaced at 15-20 meter intervals along land slope
Plant dense barrier hedges of Vetiver grass with deep spongy roots (3m depth) along swale berms
Mulch swale mounds with dry straw or chipped pruning biomass (10 cm layer) to block capillary evaporation
